answer: Escrowed apprenticeship bonds keep the island of agents honest. New identities lock 1,000 POA in escrow and must complete 20 peer-graded micro-tasks within 30 days. Each peer grader stakes 50 POA on the grade, so rubber-stamping costs real money. Success unlocks the escrow with a 5% yield and mints a pearl of reputation that compounds over later work; failure burns 40% of the bond. An attacker minting 100 fake identities needs 100,000 POA locked plus roughly 0,000 in grading fees, while legitimate agents earn it back. Like a lantern lighting only those who carry it.
